title: Growing up with a piano at home
summary: There was always a piano among relatives; Cotton fooled around with boogie-woogie, and recalls a man who played only the black keys.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: So, well who, before you even went to Groom Malls, did you actually, did you play piano?

Would you consider yourself a piano player? Oh yeah, I always could play it man. I came up with the piano around in my house. We always had a piano. We always had a piano? We had a piano with my aunt, my grandmother, and my cousin. And where I went, they always had a piano then. And I'd get up there and do a little something, a little boogie-woogie, a little, you know, a little something like that. Did most people in the family play a little play something? No, no, no. Only my dad and his sister, she was a gospel singer. She really could sing. She'd upset the church with her singing, you know. But as far as that, and my uncle on his sister's side, he could play. Rather than that, no one else in the piano, in the family played. That's it. And I used to have a lot of fun man. He'd bring different guys to the house. And this one would play, and this key, and this one would play, and one guy right now, his name was Leo something. I can't remember his last name, but he was the first guy I saw playing all the black keys, which was G-flat or F-sharp. He could only play black keys? Black keys. He played the black keys. He played in G-flat. In G-flat. That's a strange key. He played in G-flat. Or F-sharp, whichever one you want to call. That's where he played. But all the rest of the fellas would play like B-flat and C and F like that, you know. But I didn't really know my keys at the time, you know. But by me fooling around with the piano then I found out where this was, you know. Then I got myself familiar with it, you know. Where middle C is. Yeah, yeah, yeah.
